Chief executive officer of the Armani Group, effective immediately, with a board seat, reporting to the board chaired by Leo Dell'Orco; a long-time manager who had supported Armani in global management since 2019 (FashionUnited 2025-10-16). Predecessor is the founder, who ran the company until his death on 2025-09-04; his own title is not stated in the source. Business Today (2026-09-17) calls Marsocci CEO and Managing Director of the Armani Group.

Also called Leo Rongone; leaves Bottega Veneta on 2026-03-31 (see bottega_veneta rows). Remo Ruffini stepped down as chief executive to become executive chairman, retaining responsibility for creative direction (FashionNetwork 2026-01-20 and 2026-01-21). Group level: no separate Moncler brand chief executive is named in the sources read, and FashionNetwork (2026-05-26) calls Rongone CEO of the Moncler Group since 1 April; Stone Island is outside this row.

FashionNetwork (2016-10-03) says new boss Eraldo Poletto arrived 'last August', i.e. August 2016, and names him CEO in 2017 (FashionNetwork 2017-10-05); announcement date not found. Michele Norsa was chief executive when Giornetti left in March 2016 (FashionUnited 2016-03-28).

Named as CEO in February 2019 (FashionUnited 2019-02-21); she joined Ferragamo from Gucci in April 2018 according to her LinkedIn profile, as cited by FashionUnited Germany (2021-06-28). When she became CEO, and whether she directly succeeded Eraldo Poletto, were not confirmed, so the dates and predecessor are blank.

Announced Monday 2021-06-28, leaving Burberry at the end of 2021 (FashionUnited Germany); a FashionUnited Germany headline of 2021-11-10 says he starts at the beginning of January, so start_date is the month. Called CEO in March 2022 (FashionUnited Germany 2022-03-14). Whether he has been succeeded since was not checked: the web search budget ran out.
'Schulte first took on the role in November of 2016' (FashionNetwork 2019-10-31); predecessor not named.
Resignation reported 2019-10-31, citing WWD; no replacement named, while Fabrizio Fabbro joined as chief operating officer (FashionNetwork).
Reported 2023-01-20; 'she will helm the brand', according to US fashion media (FashionNetwork). Start date and predecessor not stated. Formerly CEO of PVH Americas and Calvin Klein Global.

Appointed CEO 'effective May, 2022', succeeding Emmanuel Gintzburger, who was leaving Kering; reporting to François-Henri Pinault (FashionUnited, published 2022-03-21; The Impression 2022-03-21; Retail Bulletin 2022-03-22: 'due to take up his role in May'). Previously president of EMEA and VP global retail at Gucci, having joined Kering in 2016 as president of Gucci for Greater China. Succeeded by Gianfranco D'Attis on 2026-06-03 (next row); he had decided to leave Kering later in 2026 (Retail Bulletin 2026-06-03).

Appointed CEO in 2020, having joined at the beginning of that year from Zadig & Voltaire (FashionNetwork 2024-03-18); exact dates and predecessor not stated. Earlier Balmain chief executives in the window were not checked.
Stepped down after four years 'to pursue other interests'; no successor named then (FashionNetwork 2024-03-18).

Joined from Givenchy, where he was international director (FashionUnited Germany 2024-04-16). Still CEO in November 2025 (Reuters via MarketScreener, 2025-11-12) and on 2026-10-09: 'The house is currently led by chief executive officer Matteo Sgarbossa' (FashionNetwork, https://us.fashionnetwork.com/news/Balmain-unveils-new-300-square-metre-flagship-boutique-in-milan,1874695.html). FashionNetwork's Balmain tag page, read 2026-10-15, lists no CEO change since his appointment.

FashionNetwork names her CEO on 2018-12-13 and on 2021-10-08 ('led by CEO Delphine Bellini', https://ca.fashionnetwork.com/news/Schiaparelli-kickstarts-retail-operations-with-first-store-in-US,1342344.html). Puck (page undated) says she was recruited 'as C.E.O. in 2014'; the IFM faculty page says she joined Schiaparelli's general management in May 2014, but IFM is not a trade or company source and Puck gives only the year, so start_date is blank. Camilla Schiavone had been named CEO in June 2012 (TextilWirtschaft 2012-06-19); whether Bellini directly succeeded her is not stated, so predecessor is blank. No successor found; the latest dated source read naming her CEO is from October 2021.

At Lanvin since 2008, deputy managing director from 2011 to 2013, CEO from 2013, replacing Thierry Andretta, who had led the brand since 2009 (FashionNetwork 2017-09-14). In September 2017 she was giving up the CEO post to return to deputy managing director and was about to leave the board; Nicolas Druz followed (next row). The sources give only the year 2013, so start_date is blank. CEO in October 2015 (FashionNetwork 2015-10-28, the existing source).

Shaw-Lan Wang brought him in as adviser at the end of August 2017 as Michèle Huiban gave up the CEO post (FashionNetwork 2017-09-14); in December 2017 he was 'General Manager and advisor to Shaw-Lan Wang', with Huiban as deputy general manager (FashionNetwork 2017-12-21); WWD (2018-02-26, reproduced by Vendome Global Partners) says Wang 'subsequently brought back Nicolas Druz as chief executive officer', succeeding Huiban. When he took the top title was not stated. He stepped down as Lanvin CEO on 2018-03-22, after Fosun's takeover (FashionNetwork 2018-03-22, the existing source).
Appointed interim CEO after Fosun's acquisition of Lanvin (FashionNetwork 2018-03-22).

Naming him CEO was 'one of FFG's first moves after acquiring control of Lanvin' (in spring 2018), and he hired Bruno Sialelli; formerly at Tag Heuer and for eight years at Louis Vuitton. He left 'effective immediately' on 2020-03-17 in a management overhaul, with Joann Cheng taking over as interim CEO (FashionNetwork 2020-03-17; next row). CEO in January 2019 (FashionNetwork 2019-01-21). Lanvin announced his appointment as chief executive, after four years at Sandro, in a statement on Tuesday 2018-08-28 (FashionUnited 2018-08-28), so announced_date is that day; his start date was not stated; Joann Cheng had been interim CEO since 2018-03-22 (existing row), so predecessor is left blank.

Appointed deputy general manager, succeeding Arnaud Bazin, to take over 'at the end of the year', reporting to Joann Cheng (FashionNetwork and FashionUnited, both 2021-12-07; announced_date is the report date); he joined Lanvin in December 2021 from Theory (The Impression 2026-03-14). Called deputy CEO by 2024 (FashionNetwork 2024-06-27, existing note); departure reported 2026-03-13 (existing departure row).
Reported by multiple outlets on Friday 2026-03-13 (FashionNetwork 2026-03-16); no successor named. Andy Lew continues to oversee the brand (next row).

In March 2026 he was executive president of Lanvin Group and chairman and CEO of the brand (FashionNetwork 2026-03-16; The Impression 2026-03-14). Announcement date and predecessor not found.

Named CEO, joining on 21 October 2019 from Moschino, where he had been general manager until the previous month, succeeding Frederick Lukoff (Modaes 2019-10-08; announced_date is the report date). He 'joined the company in 2019 as both president and CEO' (FashionUnited 2023-11-24) and was 'leaving after four years at the helm' (World Footwear 2023-12-05), stepping down in December 2023 as Amandine Ohayon took over from 2023-12-01 (The Industry 2023-11-24); his exact last day was not given.

Appointed CEO effective 1 December 2023, succeeding Gabriele Maggio, based in London and reporting to the board (The Industry 2023-11-24; FashionUnited 2023-11-24, which says WWD reported it first; announced_date is the report date). Previously CEO of Pronovias from March 2018 to August 2023. She left after almost two years, when Tom Mendenhall was named CEO (FashionNetwork 2025-09-08, the existing source); her last day was not found.
Reported 2025-09-08; formerly president of the Polo and Double RL brand at Ralph Lauren and COO at Tom Ford. Start date not stated (FashionNetwork).

Promotion reported 2018-10-24, effective 2018-10-01; the article does not name the legal entity. Nagatani stayed on in an advisory role (FashionNetwork). A FashionNetwork headline on Issey Miyake Inc. appointing a new global chief executive could not be opened, so that change is not recorded.

Ferragamo's release of 2025-02-03 (issued at 18:14 after that day's board meeting): employment and directorship ended by mutual agreement, effective 2025-03-06, the date the 2024 draft accounts were approved; the company began selecting a new CEO under its succession plan and named no successor (also FashionNetwork 2025-02-03 and FashionUnited 2025-02-04). Executive powers passed to the chairman, Leonardo Ferragamo, with a transition advisory committee of James Ferragamo, Ernesto Greco and Michele Norsa (FashionNetwork 2025-02-03); he is not a chief executive, so he has no row of his own. Still without a permanent chief executive on 2026-08-03 (FashionNetwork); FashionNetwork's Ferragamo tag page, read 2026-10-15, shows no CEO appointment since.

Kering appointed him chief executive of Alexander McQueen, reporting to Grita Loebsack, Kering's chief executive of couture and leather goods emerging brands (Retail Bulletin, 2016-05-05; announced_date is the report date). He had been worldwide retail and wholesale director of Yves Saint Laurent from 2011 to 2016. Start date and predecessor are not stated: the source does not mention Jonathan Akeroyd, whose Versace appointment was reported on 2016-05-23 (versace rows). CEO 'since 2016' until 2022, when he left for Versace (The Impression 2022-03-21).

Kering announced that he 'has become the new chief executive of Alexander McQueen', effective from 3 June (Retail Bulletin, 2026-06-03; announced_date is the report date). Most recently chief executive of Prada, earlier at LVMH and Richemont; based in London, reporting to Kering CEO Luca de Meo. Testa, CEO for the previous four years, had decided to leave Kering later in the year. One trade source read; Kering's own release was not found.

Named CEO 'effective immediately', succeeding Emmanuel Diemoz; the story broke on WWD on the morning of 2017-04-03 (FashionUnited; also FashionNetwork 2017-04-03, https://us.fashionnetwork.com/news/Balmain-names-massimo-piombini-new-ceo,812474.html). Previously worldwide commercial director of Valentino, Balmain's sister company under Mayhoola, and already on Balmain's board. When he left, and whether Jean-Jacques Guével (CEO from 2020) succeeded him directly, were not found.

role: Co-Chief Executive Officer (co-gérant) of Hermès International
notes: Person in the role in 2014; no new chief executive appointment since. Appointed co-gérant by the Management Board of Émile Hermès SARL, effective 4 June 2013 (Hermès press release, 4 June 2013); the Hermès 2013 Annual Report gives 'Since 5 June 2013'. The succession was first announced on 29 May 2012 (Hermès press release, AMF filing FCCNS110911_20120529: Émile Hermès SARL 'nommera en juin 2013' Axel Dumas co-gérant). Patrick Thomas held office 'Until 31 January 2014' (2013 Annual Report, AMF FCCNS126529_20140610) and 'stepped down as Executive Chairman with effect from 31 January 2014' (press release of 21 March 2014, AMF FCCNS124174_20140325). From then on Dumas has been the sole individual Executive Chairman; Modaes (3 Feb 2014) reported him sole CEO 'desde hoy'. Current listings (MarketScreener; Simply Wall St) still show him in the role in 2026. The other gérant is the corporate general partner Émile Hermès SARL (now SAS), represented by Henri-Louis Bauer since 1 July 2012 (2012 Annual Report, AMF FCCNS117936_20130522); no change found there either.

Modaes (23 Jan 2020) states he 'tomará el cargo de presidente de la marca el próximo 1 de febrero'; FashionNetwork (24 Jan 2020) also gives a 1 February start. The role was new: FashionUnited (13 Dec 2021) says he 'was appointed to the newly created role of president in January last year'. No chief executive or managing director of Dries Van Noten was found for 2014-2019. In that period the founder ran the house; after Puig took a majority stake in June 2018 he 'will continue as Chief Creative Officer and Chairman of the Board' (Puig press release). De Rosa left in December 2021 to become CEO of LVMH Métiers d'Art.

Former Jil Sander CEO. TheIndustry.fashion and FashionNetwork are both dated 10 Dec 2021; Modaes and FashionUnited ran it on 13 Dec 2021. No start date is stated; De Rosa was 'leaving mid December to head up LVMH Métiers d'Art'. FashionNetwork calls De Rosa 'CEO' where other outlets say president. FashionNetwork (28 Apr 2025) still calls Keller 'president of Dries Van Noten'. No later change found in searches or on FashionNetwork's Dries Van Noten tag page (latest executive item: Julian Klausner named creative director).

No chief executive or president appointment found for Max Mara Fashion Group since 2014; this is the person heading the group in 2014, with no change found. BoF profile: 'Chairman, Max Mara', 'at the helm of the company since the passing of his father' (founder Achille Maramotti died in January 2005, per FashionUnited 18 Jan 2005). No appointment date is stated, hence verified=false. Sources disagree on the title: chairman (Wikipedia, citing WWD 5 Nov 2013); 'the house's CEO' (FashionNetwork, 6 Jun 2018); 'Chief Executive' (TheIndustry.fashion company profile, modified 12 Nov 2021). A 2007 TextilWirtschaft article called Ignazio Maramotti 'Konzernpräsident'. Not recorded as appointments: (1) TheOfficialBoard lists 'Riccardo Broggi (CEO)' at Max Mara Fashion Group, with no news or company source found to back it; (2) a Kyiv university page (5 Feb 2025) calls Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti 'Chairman of the Board of Directors', but Marie Claire (May 2026) calls her a board member, on the board since 2019. The company is private, and maxmarafashiongroup.com could not be fetched.
